items.title: John Levy interviewed by Monk Rowe, Majesty of the Seas, May 31, 1995
items.q: I did sign up people like Ahmad Jamal, Ramsey Lewis, that was one of the first things.

ctx.x: Okay, well we won’t date you with that.

Remember it all, but anyway, that was my first person to sign up as a manager. And then I said, I was only thinking in terms of musicians anyway. I didn’t know too much about singers and I didn’t, you know that wasn’t my cup of tea was the way I felt about it at that time. So we, I did sign up people like Ahmad Jamal, Ramsey Lewis, that was one of the first things. And by this time George Shearing was on Capitol Records by this time. And that’s a whole other story, how we got on that. I just walked into the…

items.title: John Levy — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: Originally I did have agreements – written agreements with Ahmad Jamal, with Ramsey Lewis.

ctx.x: . . . Shirley Scott, Cannonball, Billy Taylor, and Ahmad Jamal. They were the initial wave of artists who came in to John Levy Enterprises. How did they – how did you make arrangements with them? Because you had a reputation of not having contracts or making a deal with a handshake.

That came about maybe a little bit later. Originally I did have agreements – written agreements with Ahmad Jamal, with Ramsey Lewis. But I soon found out that it didn’t make any difference. This is why I changed that complete thing and just said, look – because it’s like a marriage. If you’re not going to respect each other and you’re not going to get along, and you have no respect for each other, then I feel that you can’t work together. You can’t do anything constructive. It can only be a lot of hassles with…

I did other things with Ramsey Lewis later on, after the separation, but I never got involved in his career any more after that. I didn’t – we both were on Columbia Records, and he did some things with Nancy [Wilson], because he and Nancy became close friends. That how – it was a continuation of me having anything to do with Ramsey Lewis from that point on.
